parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment addresses the paper's discussion of hyper-parameter tuning methodologies and reproducibility, explicitly referencing the reporting of tuning methodology and the released code. Since the paper's stated aim is increasing reproducibility through reporting hyper-parameter tuning methodologies, this target should be obvious to the authors, even though the comment does not name a specific section, table, or figure. The rubric allows grounding either through explicit mention of a part or when the referenced part is obvious to the authors; here the comment satisfies the grounding requirement because the referenced area is clearly identifiable to the authors. Additionally, the comment is highly specific: it asks two concrete questions about whether the same 20% validation split was used across experiments, whether it can be released, and whether a single split or cross-validation was used, clearly specifying what needs to be addressed. The comment thus both points to an identifiable part of the paper and details the issues in that part. The original assessment that the authors cannot confidently identify the referenced part is not supported, since the comment explicitly names the topic (tuning methodology reporting) and the released code, making the target unambiguous.

change_log.reason: The comment does identify a specific aspect of the paper, and the rubric allows grounding when the referenced part is obvious to the authors, not only via explicit section pointers.

change_log.reason: The comment's explicit mention of tuning methodology and released code makes the target identifiable, so the claim of imprecise identification is a factual error, and the grounding conclusion is stated affirmatively rather than left open.
